summary: Lycoming County, PA wooden tower built 1916 and no longer standing per the FFLOS register; no removal date, staffing or present-day source found.

facts.status_note: The register says the tower is no longer standing and gives no removal date. No source describes what remains today.

events.note: Register says the wooden tower was built in 1916

notes_for_editor: One source: the FFLOS register entry, which gives the 1916 wooden build, that the tower is no longer standing, and the 2008 registration. Two web searches and three page reads (Tiadaghton State Forest history, a Shaffers Path lookout page and a Wikipedia Red Ridge page) found nothing about this tower. The neighbouring Red Ridge Point Tower Site (US 443, PA 272) is a separate register entry and is not merged here; it needs its own record. The story is short because the evidence is short, and it says plainly that no source describes the site today. Confidence low.
